purpose: Section 14 red-team pass against src/klpga/neo_win/pre_5prob.py and scripts/104_pre_5prob_backtest.py.

future_leakage.evidence: PreSimInput has no field a real, already-played round score could occupy (test_simulate_pre_tournament_never_uses_a_real_round_score_as_input); ALL 4 rounds are drawn from the frozen PRE prior in every trial.

survivorship_bias.evidence: OK Open's backtest field is CUT_SURVIVORS_ONLY (68 of ~120) because OK_OPEN_2026_POST_R2_FINAL_FORECAST.json only carries PRE-time features for players who survived the real cut. Disclosed in NEO_PRE_5PROB_BACKTEST_V1.json's field_completeness field and factored into the publication gate's FIELD_INTEGRITY=PARTIAL verdict -- not hidden, not fixed by fabricating missing-player features.

unequal_exposure.evidence: Every player without a real score/spread falls back to the SAME population-mean convention already used by round_update.py -- no player gets a different fallback rule than another.

missed_cut_bias.evidence: KG's field includes real missed-cut players (n_missed_cut=56); OK's reduced field cannot exercise this at all (n_missed_cut=0) -- same finding as survivorship_bias above.

wd_handling.evidence: KG's official leaderboard includes WD players (e.g. player_id 9750, rounds=[null,null,null,null]); these are correctly excluded from actual_rank_by_id (rank_numeric=null) and correctly scored as not-made-cut, with no crash or silent miscount.

field_strength_distortion.evidence: i.i.d. per-round Normal draws, no course-difficulty correlation -- identical, already-disclosed simplification to round_update.py's own docstring. Not newly introduced by this module.

small_samples.evidence: N=2 historical events -- already the primary reason NEO_PRE_5PROB_PUBLICATION_GATE_V1.json is BLOCKED_INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE. This is the single most important red-team finding and it is not being talked around.

duplicate_player_codes.evidence: Neither KG's (120) nor OK's (68) real field rows contained a duplicate player_code in this pass -- build_pre_sim_inputs would silently let a later duplicate's dict entry win in simulate_pre_tournament's result dict if one existed; not hardened defensively since no real duplicate was ever observed in this codebase's player_code usage elsewhere.

monotonicity.evidence: any_monotonicity_violation=false for both real backtest events; tests/test_pre_5prob.py additionally checks this on synthetic data with an intentionally adversarial field.

overconfidence_and_winner_concentration.reason: Requires a real calibration analysis across many events -- N=2 cannot support this claim either way; deferred to whatever real walk-forward backtest eventually unblocks MODEL_VALIDATION.

tournament_specific_hardcoding.evidence: src/klpga/neo_win/pre_5prob.py contains zero tournament-specific literals -- it accepts arbitrary field_rows. scripts/104_pre_5prob_backtest.py DOES reference KG/OK by name, but this is a historical-reproduction/backtest script (same convention as the existing two-event validation harness), not the generic production pipeline.

changes_made_as_a_result: None to pre_5prob.py's model semantics -- every finding above was either already correctly handled or is a disclosed, evidenced BLOCK rather than a bug to silently patch. No formula was tuned to make a finding go away.
